gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states a measured power draw with all three cameras recording: DashCamTalk testers measured about 7.1 W for the Vantrue N4S (4.3 W in low-bitrate parking), 6.16 W for the Viofo A229 Plus 3CH (5.71 W parking) and 7.95 W for the A229 Pro 3CH (6.25 W parking), and the N4 Pro S tester cites a 9 W figure.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible's 3-channel guide (rank 1, cited; specs from maker pages and manuals only, no measurement), Digital Camera World's 3-channel guide (specs only in the part returned; Alistair Charlton fits units to his car but gives no figures) and Notebookcheck's N4 Pro S review (Stephen Pereyra; spec-sheet values, no power, heat or bitrate readings). Vortex Radar's best-dash-cams page (cited in both chats) returned HTTP 403 and ezdashcam.com returned HTTP 429, so I could not check either; Vortex Radar tests cameras itself, which is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms the pick more than it changes it. The Vantrue N4 Pro S is the heaviest draw of the group if the 9 W figure is its 3-channel driving load (the tester's text does not name the mode), so it runs a parking battery down fastest. The N4S's measured 4.3 W low-bitrate parking draw backs it as the value pick for someone parking on a battery pack; the tester estimated about 60 hours on a 276 Wh pack. The Viofo A229 Plus 3CH draws 1.79 W less than the A229 Pro 3CH while driving (7.95 − 6.16) and ran 16 °C cooler in the same tester's 3-channel comparison, which matters in a hot car. The figures come from different testers, supply voltages (12.60 V and 15.76 V) and channel settings, so the Vantrue and Viofo numbers are indicative side by side, not a like-for-like ranking.

findings.label: Power draw, driving, front + cabin + rear recording (EricSan, DashCamTalk, post #25, 2025-06-15)
findings.value: about 452 mA at 15.76 V, about 7.1 W
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum, page 2)
findings.note: Multimeter in series with the hardwire kit's negative lead, min/max over about 20 s (478 mA max, 427 mA min, averaged); supply was a full LTO parking battery at 15.76 V. 0.452 A × 15.76 V = 7.12 W. EricSan calls it 'not a super precise measurement'. The row is labelled 'all 1440P' in the prose I was given; the table itself is an image I could not read, so check the front-camera resolution for that row. Other rows: front + cabin 472 mA (about 7.4 W), front + rear 440 mA (about 6.9 W), front only 432 mA (about 6.8 W). Vantrue's manual rating is 7 W, as quoted in the post.

findings.label: Power draw, low-bitrate parking mode, front + rear at 1080p (EricSan, DashCamTalk, 2025-06-15)
findings.value: about 275 mA typical at 15.76 V, about 4.3 W
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum, page 2)
findings.note: 393 mA max and 158 mA min, averaged. This is two channels (front + rear), not three. EricSan estimates about 60 hours of parking recording on a 276 Wh LTO battery (276 ÷ 4.3 = 64 h before losses).

findings.label: Bitrate per channel with three channels recording (EricSan, DashCamTalk, posts #1 and #16, 2025-06-11 to 13)
findings.value: front 2592×1944 at 16.0 Mb/s, cabin 1440p at 14.3 Mb/s, rear 1440p at 14.3 Mb/s, all 30 fps; parking mode 1920×1080 at 15 fps, 4,915 kb/s per camera
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Post #1 writes the rear as 2592×1440 and post #16 as 2560×1440. Post #16 gives a 3-minute parking file as 112,640 kB per camera. Firmware version not stated.

findings.label: Power draw (EricSan, DashCamTalk, post #68, 2025-07-26)
findings.value: 9 W, mode not named in the text
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk forum, page 4)
findings.note: Exact sentence: 'Given the 9w power consumption figure, I'm presuming this is why the new utility outlet power supply is rated to 3A.' Multimeter between the hardwire kit's negative leg and a bench supply, each reading averaged over about 30 s. The per-mode table is an image ('N4 Pro S Power Consumption.webp') I could not read, so do not print 9 W as the 3-channel driving figure without opening that image.

findings.label: Hottest surface temperature (Hack_man, DashCamTalk, post #2, 2025-07-18)
findings.value: 130.1 °F (54.5 °C) directly below the cabin lens, at 77.0 °F (25 °C) ambient
findings.note: IR thermometer gun, camera powered for more than 30 minutes, recording 2 channels at full resolution (not all three). Rise over ambient 53.1 °F (29.5 °C).

findings.label: Bitrate per channel (EricSan, DashCamTalk, posts dated 2025-07-20 to 22)
findings.value: front 3840×2160 at 30 fps, 31.9 Mb/s (236,202 kB per minute); rear 1440p at 30 fps, 14.3 Mb/s (107,178 kB per minute); cabin 1920×1080 at 30 fps, 74,410 kB per minute
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: 74,410 kB/min × 8 ÷ 60 = about 9.9 Mb/s for the cabin camera. The text I was given read '0.98 Mb/s', which does not match that file size, so use the file size. The reader noted these as per-channel figures and could not confirm they were taken with all three recording. The thread lists the rear sensor as IMX678; Dealectric's record from Vantrue says IMX675. EricSan also notes the supercapacitor gives 3 to 4 seconds of runtime after power is removed, and that his unit may be pre-release.
